weak_claims_to_deep_research.claim_text: Post-MCU follow-up non-compliance rate for non-urgent findings in Indonesia/Malaysia employer MCU context is 30-60%; estimated 108-180 employees per 1,000-employee campaign fail to present for care after abnormal MCU finding
weak_claims_to_deep_research.issue: All proxy sources are Singapore, French, and Japanese data. No Indonesia- or Malaysia-specific MCU post-screening follow-up compliance study found. Explicitly tagged [ASSUMED-8]. The 30-60% leakage estimate is the core quantitative claim for the highest-clinical-stakes pain point (PP4.3) and is used to calculate a MYR 324,000-1,440,000 employer cost figure. Geography mismatch override on all three sources.
weak_claims_to_deep_research.suggested_action: Search for Malaysia-specific occupational health follow-up compliance data. Candidate sources: (1) DOSH Malaysia annual report or USECHH statistics on follow-up outcome tracking; (2) Institute for Public Health (IPH) Malaysia reports on NCD screening follow-up in workplace settings; (3) SOCSO/PERKESO occupational disease surveillance data; (4) Naluri Malaysia or BookDoc internal cohort data (request via partnership/interview). Search query: 'Malaysia workplace health screening follow-up compliance rate employer site:dosh.gov.my OR site:nih.gov.my OR site:moh.gov.my'. Secondary search: 'ASEAN occupational health periodic examination follow-up compliance site:pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov'.

gate_reasoning: Stage 4 scores 0 High, 0 Medium, and 46 Low (100%) across all claims. The dominant structural problem is that nearly every claim in this stage rests on a single source, which triggers the Low ceiling regardless of that source's category. Several additional overrides compound this: four claims cite vendor marketing pages as primary evidence (auto-low-vendor), two market sizing claims rely solely on Grand View Research (auto-low-aggregator), seven claims are explicitly tagged [ASSUMED-N], eight claims use Singapore/French/Japanese/US data as proxies for Indonesia/Malaysia without stated equivalence (geography mismatch), three salary-basis claims have URL-to-claim category mismatches (nurse and GP salary URLs used to evidence admin salary figures), and the BPJS expenditure figure is unverifiable due to a paywall. The most commercially critical weak claim — the 30-60% MCU follow-up leakage rate underpinning PP4.3's cost calculation — has no Indonesia- or Malaysia-specific evidence at all and is built entirely from non-analogous geography proxies. Pass-3 deep research is recommended with priority targets: (1) ID/MY occupational health follow-up compliance rate from DOSH Malaysia, IPH Malaysia, or Naluri cohort data; (2) official BPS Indonesia and DOSM Malaysia labor statistics for admin and occupational physician wages; (3) multilateral or government cross-validation for the market sizing figures.
